issues.description: The problem statement and template define Rideable.messageOnRide() as a no-argument method returning a String (UML and example usage in Main call r.messageOnRide()), but the solution defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) (with an int parameter) and implements the method accordingly in Pig and Seal. This parameter mismatch is structural and will confuse students: the template / problem expect a no-arg method and show calls without arguments, while the solution enforces a different signature with an int parameter.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable interface consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to match the problem/template by removing the int parameter: define Rideable.messageOnRide():String and update Pig and Seal implementations to a no-arg messageOnRide() returning e.g. "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]", or (B) if the intended design requires a speed parameter, update the problem statement UML and template Main usage to declare and call messageOnRide(int speed) and adapt examples accordingly. Preferred fix: align solution to the no-arg signature in the problem/template.

issues.description: The Problem Statement and Template expect a no-argument method messageOnRide():String (see UML and example usage in Main), but the Solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and implements messageOnRide(int) in Pig and Seal. This changes the method signature and return format (solution includes speed), breaking the one-to-one mapping between the described API and the solution implementation and causing confusion about how to call and implement the ride behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem and template: change Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) to messageOnRide() in solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Rideable.java and update Pig and Seal to implement the no-argument messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". Alternatively, if speed is required, update the problem statement and template to declare messageOnRide(int speed) and adjust examples accordingly — but keep names and signatures consistent across all artifacts.
